explanation: Resigning mid-meeting before hearing the answer, and regretting it within hours, is acting rashly without thought, which is what impetuous names.

explanation: Arriving early and waiting is offered as proof against laziness, so the blank has to be the accusation being denied, which is indolent.
stem: The staff were not _____ so much as unled: they arrived early, sat down at their desks, and waited for instructions that never came.

explanation: Losing cellars rather than houses is severity reduced rather than removed, which is what mitigate says; aggravate and exacerbate would mean worse damage.
stem: Nothing could undo the flood, but sandbags and an early warning did _____ the damage, and the town lost cellars rather than houses.

explanation: Expense claims and an unringing telephone are the ordinary and unexciting side of the job, which is what mundane names; arduous would make it hard rather than dull.
stem: For all the talk of espionage, most of the work was _____: filing expense claims, booking flights, and waiting for a telephone that rarely rang.

explanation: Agreeing with two directors at once is servile eagerness to please, which obsequious names, while imperious and haughty describe the opposite posture.

explanation: Nine months of identical refusals is a refusal to move at all, which obstinate names; amenable, docile and tractable all describe someone who would have bent.

stem: The charter's key clause is so _____ that even the two lawyers who drafted it cannot explain its effect without resorting to a diagram.

explanation: Three pages on a comma and nothing on a collapsing argument is fuss over trivia at the cost of what matters, which is exactly pedantic.

explanation: Resilience and lessons learned, offered instead of answers, are dull overused remarks, which platitude names; an epigram or aphorism would at least be pointed.
stem: The statement offered one _____ after another about resilience and lessons learned, and answered none of the three questions the inquiry had asked.

explanation: The contrast between an ideal city and what can be built by spring is the clue: she is judging by what works rather than by theory, which is what pragmatic names.
stem: Her approach to the housing shortage was resolutely _____: she asked not what an ideal city would look like, but what could actually be built by spring.

explanation: One sentence that sets off a bank run has caused it suddenly, which is what precipitate means; avert would mean the run never happened.
stem: A single sentence in the governor's speech was enough to _____ a run on the bank that took three weeks and a federal loan to stop.

explanation: Advising on a funeral after two meetings is overstepping what the acquaintance allows, which presumptuous names; deferential and diffident would mean holding back.

explanation: A reputation that survives accusations of wrongdoing is one for uprightness rather than mere frankness, and probity is the word for that integrity.
stem: Thirty years on the bench had earned him a reputation for _____ that survived even the accusations made by his last opponent.

explanation: A title and an office with no duties attached is precisely a sinecure, a position that pays without asking for work.

explanation: Three meetings one month and none the next describes an irregular pattern rather than a hasty or difficult one, which is what sporadic says.
stem: The committee's meetings were so _____ that summer, three in May and none at all in June, that nobody could remember what had last been decided.

stem: Witnesses expected the defendant to flinch when the sentence was read, but he remained _____, wearing the same blank expression he had for six weeks.

stem: Cheap sensors did not merely assist the old survey method; within five years they had begun to _____ it in every commercial practice.

explanation: Three conversations in ten years, and silence even at his own party, describes a habit of saying very little, which is exactly taciturn; the rest describe talkers.

explanation: A statue and an endowed lecture are acts of deep respect, which venerate names, and they reverse the vilifying the town once did.

explanation: Doors onto walls and giant benches are playful inventions that raise a laugh, which is what whimsical describes.
